name: Redpoint Ventures
history: Redpoint Ventures was founded in 1999 in Menlo Park by six partners who left two firms at once: Brad Jones, Jeff Brody and Tim Haley from Brentwood Venture Capital, and Geoff Yang, Tom Dyal and John Walecka from Institutional Venture Partners. The two firms' information-technology practices combined into Redpoint while their healthcare and life-science practices went the other way into Versant Ventures, and the partners' pre-1999 deals stayed behind: the firm's own early site carried them in a separate table headed 'Previous Investments by Redpoint Partners'. Redpoint raised a $600M first fund in 1999 and a $1.25B second fund in 2000, invested through the telecom and optical bust, and rebuilt around consumer internet and infrastructure. It added a growth sleeve, Redpoint Omega, in 2007, a China effort in 2005 that became a separate firm in 2015, and a Brazilian joint venture with e.ventures in 2012. The firm moved from 3000 Sand Hill Road to Woodside in 2022 and today runs two fund lines side by side, the early-stage Redpoint Ventures series (X, $650M, 2025) and the growth-stage Redpoint Omega series (V, $740M, 2024).
investment_concept: Two vehicles, one partnership: an early-stage fund that leads seed and Series A rounds and a growth fund that enters at Series B and later, with the same partners working both. The firm publishes a one-line entry claim on every company page — 'We first partnered for their Series C in 2012' — which makes its own stage discipline unusually legible: 58% of the base entered at Series A, 13% at seed, 28% at growth.
